What the measurements show

The checked-in analytical model generally predicts fewer cycles than the hardware records. Across the included observations, signed cycle bias is -13.02%. Median absolute percentage error is 40.62%; 2.98% of individual predictions fall within ±10% of measured cycles.

These are timing errors, not failed matrix outputs: all included operations have saved numerical PASS results. The model was not fitted, calibrated or edited for this report.

Small-output cases (M≤20) have 36.05% MAPE across 3,730 observations. Large native cases (K≥256 and M≥256) have 20.71% MAPE across 266 observations. These groups differ in suite, precision, design and repetition, so this is a descriptive comparison rather than proof of a single cause.

Do not interpret “100 − MAPE” as a success rate. MAPE, WAPE and balanced MAPE are different error measures. TC08 contains 2,592 observations of only 18 design/shape/precision workloads; per-measurement summaries therefore give those workloads much more influence. The balanced figure gives each distinct workload equal weight.

Method and matching parameters

Reference timing is the active accelerator-stage total: Load X + Generate + combined Load W/Select + Store O. Separate Load W and Select counters overlap and are not added again. CPU rdcycle intervals, simulated CPU printing/copies, Python reference work, wall-clock runtime and simulator startup are not used as reference cycles.

compute_cycles(Rin=1, Cin=actual_K, Cout=actual_M,
    in_bits=16, w_bits=actual_weight_bits, XS=actual_b, YS=1,
    ID=2, buffers_w=2, factor=actual_RF, DMA_WIDTH=64,
    IN_MAX=16, IN_min=8, W_MAX=8, HS=8)

Here XS maps to b and factor maps to RF. Historical configurations and runner source identify two outstanding DMA requests, 64-bit transfers, 16-bit maximum activations, and 8-bit maximum weights. The model itself forces HS=8; this report honors that behavior. The model does not use matrix values, seeds, numerical patterns, configured maximum Cin/Cout, or the W8/W4 cache flags to alter its cycle estimate.

The two original function definitions from Performance Modeling/Model.py were executed from their unmodified Python ASTs with the standard math module. Only unused top-level plotting/widget imports were omitted because their dependencies are not needed to evaluate the model. No formula or function body was changed. Original file SHA-256: 19a96da1622d43150f4b86eddd11572e2bc287f28f973b2f4991e65035bb418d.

  • Signed error = 100 × (model − HW) / HW. Negative means underprediction.
  • MAPE = mean of 100 × |model − HW| / HW over individual observations.
  • Balanced MAPE = mean of each distinct workload's mean absolute percentage error. Key: b/RF, top-level RTL revision, K, M, input precision and weight precision. Seeds and data patterns are repeated observations of that workload.
  • WAPE = 100 × sum(|model − HW|) / sum(HW); signed cycle bias = 100 × sum(model − HW) / sum(HW). WAPE does not allow positive and negative errors to cancel.
  • All 4,125 native records are counted once. The 18 Llama2 logical totals below are sums of the same native records and are not added again to global metrics.

For each valid native record, the model was evaluated at that actual operation's matrix dimensions. For LQ04, this means 62 model calls for 288×512 plus one for 288×256, then a sum—not an impossible single 32,000-output hardware invocation.

Relevant existing model assumptions

The original model includes (Cout − 2) × max(weight-load, select), repeats a uniform activation-window cost for a shorter final window, fixes DMA round-trip timing at HS=8 and does not explicitly model every FSM transition. These are visible assumptions in the original source and plausible contributors to observed differences; this report does not isolate their individual causal effects or modify them. No unsupported Cout≤2 cases occur in this comparison.

Coverage gaps: 150 operations excluded from timing accuracy

  • 53 TC01 original detailed records are unavailable.
  • Six TC10 cases timed out without completed cycles.
  • 90 later TC11 operations have a misaligned 5-bit counter selector: 72 report zero and 18 report a positive value assembled from the wrong counters. Only the first operation per fresh Verilator boot has a correctly aligned six-counter read.
  • Native 1024 W2 has no final result/cycles.

The selected scope is the canonical 180 regression, TC01–TC11, the native 1024 run and the latest completed Llama2 suite. Earlier interrupted/superseded Llama2 tile attempts, failed make attempts, unrelated GUI custom tests and extrapolated fast-mode results are outside this scope and are not counted as extra coverage.

Reproducibility and source audit

The report used saved files in the LUMAX Git checkout. It did not run new Verilator jobs, edit HW/SW sources or alter the Python model. Parser checks validated expected suite counts, per-run versus summary cycle arrays, numerical PASS status, counter-stage sums, Llama2 tile counts and cycle sums, and unique case identifiers. The completed Llama2 log explicitly records unchanged sources and restored configuration.

Two recorded top-level RTL revisions are represented: width-fixed 6bafd90926b9490d95fe8e1481631b769aef013263cdd20cb17733987e532111 (original regression and TC01), and partial-DMA-fixed 1404c50d8e37ee3d7a4967bdc95e653190cbe880bf702e1873534aba3f38434c (TC02 onward, native 1024 and completed Llama2). Revision is included in the balanced-workload key; the design tables aggregate each b/RF across available revisions.

from itertools import repeat
import math
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
from ipywidgets import interact, IntSlider, Checkbox
import seaborn as sns
from ipywidgets import SelectionSlider


def dma_finish_time_exact_bits(total_bits, ID, t_issue=1, L=6, DMA_WIDTH_bits=64, beat_time=1):
    """
    Exact finish time (cycles) to transfer total_bits when each packet = DMA_WIDTH_bits.
    - total_bits : total data size in bits
    - ID         : max outstanding requests (DMA_ID)
    - t_issue    : cycles to post one request (Tx), default 1
    - L          : round-trip latency from issue to first returned beat (HS)
    - DMA_WIDTH_bits : width in bits of one DMA packet/beat
    - beat_time  : cycles per returned beat (default 1)
    Returns finish_time in cycles (int).
    """
    if total_bits <= 0:
        return 0
    P = int(math.ceil(float(total_bits) / float(DMA_WIDTH_bits)))  # number of packets
    if P <= 0:
        return 0

    issue_time = [0.0] * P
    completion_time = [0.0] * P

    issue_time[0] = 0.0
    completion_time[0] = issue_time[0] + L  # beats_per_packet = 1 -> no extra beat delay here

    for k in range(1, P):
        earliest_issue = issue_time[k-1] + t_issue
        if k >= ID:
            earliest_issue = max(earliest_issue, completion_time[k - ID])
        issue_time[k] = earliest_issue
        completion_time[k] = issue_time[k] + L

    finish = max(completion_time)
    return int(math.ceil(finish))


def compute_cycles(
    Rin, Cin, Cout, in_bits, w_bits, XS, YS, ID,
    buffers_w=2, factor=4,
    DMA_WIDTH=64, extra_prefetch_cycles=0,
    cache_8_4=False, cache_reads=1,
    IN_MAX=16,
    IN_min=8, W_MAX=8, HS=8
):
    """
    Compute cycle and operations model for the accelerator.
    """
    HS = 8  # Handshake Protocol estimation according to verilator

    # Operations Counter (PER ACTIVATION WINDOW)
    LoadOp = 0   # Load from memory via DMA
    WriteOp = 0  # Write to memory via DMA
    AddOp = 0    # add "+" partial products
    ShiftOp = 0  # shift activations or weights
    ReadSramOp = 0  # Read from Sync Mem
    WriteSramOp = 0 # Write to Sync Mem

    # Scaling factor for activations
    factor_X = IN_MAX / in_bits

    def round_up_div(a, b):
        return (a + b - 1) // b

    # ----------------------------------------------------
    # Stage 1 - Load X (Load Activations)
    # ----------------------------------------------------

    # Cycle Modeling
    activation_block_default = (2 ** (W_MAX - w_bits))  # The maximum amount of activation blocks a memory can hold with no factors
    activation_window_per_Mem = activation_block_default * factor_X * factor # The maximum amount of activation blocks a memory can hold with factors
    activation_window_XS = min(XS * activation_window_per_Mem, Cin)
    activation_window = activation_window_XS * min(YS, Rin)

    activation_data = activation_window * in_bits
    packets_in = math.ceil(activation_data / DMA_WIDTH)
    real_ID = min(ID, packets_in)

    # compute exact DMA cycles (one packet == DMA_WIDTH bits)
    cycles_1 = dma_finish_time_exact_bits(
        total_bits=int(activation_data),
        ID=ID,
        t_issue=1,
        L=HS,
        DMA_WIDTH_bits=DMA_WIDTH,
        beat_time=1
    )

    Repeat = round_up_div(Cin, activation_window_XS) * round_up_div(Rin, min(YS, Rin))  # How many activation windows needed to complete mat-mul
    cycles_1_Total = cycles_1 * Repeat

    # Ops per activation window
    LoadOp += packets_in
    WriteSramOp += packets_in

    # ----------------------------------------------------
    # Stage 2 - Generate Products
    # ----------------------------------------------------

    # activation_per_Mem = math.ceil(min(XS * activation_window_per_Mem, Cin)  / XS)
    activation_per_Mem = min(activation_window_per_Mem,math.ceil(Cin / XS))

    #for debug
    total_padding = activation_per_Mem * XS - min(XS * activation_window_per_Mem, Cin)
    dummy_per_mem_base = total_padding // XS


    memory_blocks = XS * min(YS, Rin)
    active_activations_blocks = (activation_per_Mem / factor_X)

    cycles_2 = ((2 ** (w_bits - 2)) * active_activations_blocks + active_activations_blocks)  # Cycles needed to generate all activation products for one activation window
    cycles_2_Total = cycles_2 * Repeat

    # Ops per activation window
    ReadSramOp += (cycles_2 * memory_blocks)
    WriteSramOp += (cycles_2 * memory_blocks)
    AddOp += ((cycles_2 - 1) * memory_blocks)
    ShiftOp += activation_window  # one shift for every activation(I) to produce (2*I)

    # ----------------------------------------------------
    # Stage 3 - Load W & Select (producer–consumer model)
    # ----------------------------------------------------
    weight_elems = activation_window  # Need to load for every activation one weight from every weight matrix column
    packets_w = math.ceil((weight_elems * w_bits) / DMA_WIDTH)
    real_ID = min(ID, packets_w)

    cycles_3_1 = dma_finish_time_exact_bits(
        total_bits=int(weight_elems * w_bits),
        ID=ID,
        t_issue=1,
        L=HS,
        DMA_WIDTH_bits=DMA_WIDTH,
        beat_time=1
    )
    cycles_3_2 = 1 + (activation_per_Mem) + 2  # select & accumulate per window per column

    cycles_3_one_window = (Cout - 2) * max(cycles_3_1, cycles_3_2)
    cycles_3_Total = cycles_3_one_window * Repeat

    # Ops per activation window
    LoadOp += packets_w
    WriteSramOp += packets_w
    ReadSramOp += (cycles_3_2 * memory_blocks)
    AddOp += (cycles_3_2 * memory_blocks)
    ShiftOp += (cycles_3_2 * memory_blocks)

    # ----------------------------------------------------
    # Stage 4 - Store Output
    # ----------------------------------------------------
    output_elems = Cout * min(YS, Rin)
    O_bits = 32
    packets_0 = math.ceil((output_elems * O_bits) / DMA_WIDTH)
    real_ID = min(ID, packets_0)
    cycles_4 = dma_finish_time_exact_bits(
        total_bits=int(output_elems * O_bits),
        ID=ID,
        t_issue=1,
        L=HS,
        DMA_WIDTH_bits=DMA_WIDTH,
        beat_time=1
    )
    cycles_4_Total = cycles_4 * round_up_div(Rin, YS)

    # Ops per activation window (output write)
    WriteOp += packets_0 * round_up_div(Rin, YS)

    # ----------------------------------------------------
    # Total cycles
    # ----------------------------------------------------
    total_cycles = cycles_1_Total + cycles_2_Total + cycles_3_Total + cycles_4_Total

    return {
        'Repeat activation Window': Repeat,
        'cycles_load_X': cycles_1_Total,
        'cycles_generate_Products': cycles_2_Total,
        'cycles_loadW_select': cycles_3_Total,
        'cycles_store_output': cycles_4_Total,
        'total_cycles': total_cycles,
        'cycles load w Only': cycles_3_1 * Repeat * Cout,
        'cycles select Only': cycles_3_2 * Repeat * Cout,
        'cycles_3_1': cycles_3_1,
        'cycles_3_2': cycles_3_2,
        # Ops PER activation window:
        'LoadOp': LoadOp,
        'WriteOp': WriteOp,
        'AddOp': AddOp,
        'ShiftOp': ShiftOp,
        'ReadSramOp': ReadSramOp,
        'WriteSramOp': WriteSramOp,
    }
